rapport_notes: Amy is warm, personable, and responsive; uses customer's name naturally and matches Bailey's tone well throughout.
process_discipline_notes: No repeated differentiators; silence generally held after open-ended questions.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: "This may take five to ten minutes. Is this a good time?" — frames time but does not promise an accurate quote in return.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: "do you have any specific concern or what are you most worried about for the upcoming bailing?" — asked after Amy has already confirmed move details, dates, addresses, and square footage.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises tight stairwells and heavy furniture (300+ lbs). Amy responds: "if there's anything that we need to disassemble we can do that..." and later "I wait limit for moving items up and downstairs £300 so should be good to go." Amy addresses the concern but does not probe deeper with "tell me more" or "what else is on your list?"
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: "if there's anything that we need to disassemble we can do that if that's easier to bring those items upstairs and of course we will reassemble them as well. Whatever we disassemble and that's included in the hourly rate" — addresses carefulness indirectly but does not explicitly invoke the damage/care differentiator ("move it like it's ours," up to $2,000 coverage).
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Never mentioned. No reference to Meet Your Mover, named crew lead, or who specifically will show up.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Not covered anywhere in the call.
evidence_quotes.communication: Not covered anywhere in the call. No mention of day-before call, named crew lead, inbox updates, or any proactive communication structure.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "We charge $204 an hour that's with two movers already...we do have a two and a half hour minimum. So even if we finish the move let's say in just thirty minutes or an hour, we'll still charge you for the minimum which is $510." — gives a rate and minimum but does not anchor to a typical range for moves of this type or personalize to customer-specific factors (tight stairs, two-floor moves, etc.).
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: None of the five Save Your Ass lines are delivered. No commitment framing, no window/specificity language, no 15-min increment explanation, no self-prep tip, and no "does that feel fair?" with silence.
evidence_quotes.close: "we'll see you this coming Friday morning. Okay?" — no rate-lock line, no explicit ask (e.g., "would you like our help with your move?"). The booking is confirmed but the structured close is missing.

top_strength: Amy expertly diagnosed a logistics challenge (tight stairwells, heavy furniture) and immediately offered a concrete solution (disassembly/reassembly included in rate), which earned the customer's trust and moved to a booking without friction.
coaching_note: Stage 2 differentiators (On-Time Guarantee, Communication, Meet Your Mover) were never delivered—add the takeaway pitch after pricing to cover what the customer didn't raise, and use Save Your Ass framing (rate commitment, estimate window, self-prep tip, "does that feel fair?") before closing to lock in confidence.
